title: How the Beagle Brigade Works
summary: Josh and Chuck explain the USDA's Beagle Brigade, the beagle detection dogs that sniff agricultural products and contraband at U.S. international airports. They cover the threat of invasive species to US agriculture, the program's origins (started in Mexico, then USDA at LAX in 1994), why beagles were chosen (size, agility, approachability, prior Navy use), how dogs smell in layers, shelter-sourced dogs, the training at the National Detector Dog Training Center near Atlanta, the five basic scents, graduation and airport deployment, retirement and adoption by handlers, kenneling, and stories of seizures (roasted pig, goat head, whale meat, Jasper, Murray). They also touch on brown tree snakes in Guam and Hawaii, Burmese pythons in the Everglades, and the bushmeat smuggling pandemic risk. The episode ends with a listener email about a listener's brother and skiing with his family.

segments.title: Live tour promo and opening banter
segments.summary: Josh announces the 2017 North American Stuff You Should Know Live tour dates, then the hosts introduce the episode on the Beagle Brigade and compare it to earlier episodes on drug-sniffing and Seeing Eye dogs.
topics: Stuff You Should Know live tour

segments.title: Roasted pig smuggling and what the Beagle Brigade does
segments.summary: The hosts describe a traveler who tried to bring a whole roasted pig into Atlanta's airport, then explain that the Beagle Brigade are USDA federal agents who sniff out agricultural products to keep pests and diseases out of US agriculture, working with CBP at international airports.

segments.title: History: from Mexico to LAX in 1994
segments.summary: The program reportedly began in Mexico before the 1970s, the USDA started it in the late 1970s, and a pilot at LAX in 1994 succeeded. Before beagles, the agency used larger dogs such as German shepherds and labs, which can intimidate travelers.

segments.title: Why beagles and how dogs smell
segments.summary: The hosts compare dogs' olfactory receptors to humans', explain that beagles were chosen partly because the Navy used them and because they are small, agile and non-threatening, and describe how dogs smell scents in layers and can detect table salt at extreme dilution.

segments.title: Break
segments.summary: The hosts take a break before returning to the beagles.

segments.title: Shelter dogs, adoption and working life
segments.summary: Beagles in the program are drawn from shelters, which the USDA says would otherwise often be euthanized, and the program reportedly has a 100 percent adoption record with handlers given first right of refusal. The hosts discuss the ethics of using dogs as tools and compare with other working-dog pairings.

segments.title: Training at the National Detector Dog Training Center
segments.summary: Training takes place at the National Detector Dog Training Center near Atlanta. Dogs are screened for health, temperament and high food drive, then trained on five basic scents, with positive reinforcement. Graduates train another 10 to 13 weeks at their home airport. The hosts note the five scents are beef, pork, citrus, mango and apple, and they could not find the reason for that list.

segments.title: Airport deployment, kenneling and retirement
segments.summary: At busy airports the dogs must stay calm and non-threatening, and the vest marks them as Beagle Brigade. Dogs alert by sitting at a bag. They live in kennels near the airport rather than with handlers, and retire around age eight. The hosts discuss the retirement of Jasper, whose handler adopted him.

segments.title: Seizure stories, stats, Guam snakes, and bushmeat smuggling
segments.summary: The hosts share stories of Murray, Jasper's seizures (goat head, whale meat, rhinoceros skin, cooked bat), and annual statistics: 23 million passengers inspected and over 1.77 million seizures in 2016. They mention brown tree snakes in Guam and Hawaii, Burmese pythons in the Everglades, a declared-but-seized smuggling case, and bushmeat smuggling as a pandemic risk.

segments.title: Listener mail and sign-off
segments.summary: Josh reads a listener email from Sam about rediscovering the show through memories of skiing with her late brother and family. The hosts sign off with social media and contact information.
